narrative:
The school’s system has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s a **10% chance** you might struggle to pass your final year. While this might sound low, the system uses this threshold to identify students who could benefit from extra support—like remedial courses—to help them succeed. Think of it like a safety net: even if the risk isn’t huge, the school wants to make sure you have every opportunity to thrive.

Three key factors stood out in this decision. First, the **reason you chose this school**—reputation—played a role. Most students who don’t need extra help picked it for the course quality or because it’s close to home. When students focus more on prestige than fit, they might not engage as deeply, which can affect their performance.

Second, your **past academic record** is strong—you haven’t failed any classes before—but the system also considered your **goals for the future**. Almost all students who don’t need remedial courses plan to pursue higher education, just like you. While this might seem like a positive, the system noticed that students who are highly motivated but don’t have additional support structures sometimes face challenges balancing ambition with the workload.

The third factor is more about **support outside of school**. Unlike many peers who receive help from family or extra classes, you’re not currently getting that extra guidance. Most students who succeed have either family support or paid tutoring, which can make a big difference in staying on track.

This doesn’t mean you *will* fail—far from it. But the school wants to give you tools to ensure you don’t hit unexpected hurdles. Remedial courses will focus on strengthening areas where you might need a little extra help, like time management or specific subjects. The best next step is to take this opportunity seriously: attend the courses, ask for help when needed, and lean on any resources the school offers. You’ve got this!
